explanations: Incorrect. 48/13 is the x-coordinate of P in a coordinate setup (distance measured along AB), not the perpendicular distance from P to the line AB.
Correct. The external tangent gives AB = sqrt(13^2 - 5^2) = 12, and P divides the line of centres in the ratio 4:9, so its height is 4 + (4/13)(9-4) = 72/13.
Incorrect. 36/13 is r1*r2/(r1+r2), the product-over-sum lens value - irrelevant here; the section formula needs weighted heights, not product-over-sum.
Incorrect. 97/13 comes from swapping the section weights (4*O1 + 9*O2 instead of 9*O1 + 4*O2) when locating P.
items.prompt: Two circles of radii 4 cm and 9 cm touch each other externally at point P. A common external tangent touches the circles at A and B respectively. What is the perpendicular distance from P to the line AB?
items.solution: 1. Let O1, O2 be the centres; O1O2 = 4 + 9 = 13. 2. Drop perpendiculars O1A and O2B to the tangent; O1ABO2 is a right trapezoid with O1A = 4, O2B = 9. 3. AB^2 = O1O2^2 - (9-4)^2 = 169 - 25 = 144, so AB = 12. 4. P divides O1O2 internally in the ratio O1P:PO2 = 4:9. 5. Hence the height of P above AB is the weighted mean 4 + (4/13)(9-4) = 4 + 20/13 = 72/13. 6. Answer B.

explanations: Correct. Hypotenuse = 2R = 25; legs sum a+b = 2r+c = 31; then (a+b)^2 = a^2+b^2+2ab gives 961 = 625+2ab, so ab = 168 and area = ab/2 = 84.
Incorrect. 168 is ab, the product of the legs - shipped without the final half.
Incorrect. 42 halves twice (uses ab/4), confusing the area with a semi-area.
Incorrect. 60 assumes a scaled 6-8-10 triple, but that triple has circumradius 5, not 12.5.
items.prompt: The inradius of a right-angled triangle is 3 cm and its circumradius is 12.5 cm. Find the area of the triangle in sq cm.
items.solution: 1. For a right triangle the hypotenuse is the circumdiameter: c = 2R = 25. 2. With legs a, b: r = (a+b-c)/2, so a+b = 2*3+25 = 31. 3. Square the sum: (a+b)^2 = a^2+b^2+2ab, i.e. 961 = 625+2ab (since a^2+b^2 = c^2 = 625). 4. Thus 2ab = 336, ab = 168. 5. Area = ab/2 = 84 (check: legs 7 and 24 indeed give r = 3, R = 12.5). 6. Answer A.

explanations: Incorrect. 3 counts the distinct values of |x| (6, 2, 3) but forgets that each positive value gives two x values, + and -.
Incorrect. 4 comes from solving only the t^2-5t+6 = 0 branch (x = +2, -2, +3, -3) and missing the t = 6 branch entirely.
Correct. With t = |x| >= 0: t^2-5t = 6 gives t = 6 (t = -1 rejected), and t^2-5t = -6 gives t = 2, 3. So x = +6, -6, +2, -2, +3, -3: six values.
Incorrect. 2 comes from solving only the t^2-5t-6 = 0 branch and then dropping t = -1 without counting x = +6 and -6.
items.prompt: How many real values of x satisfy |x^2 - 5|x|| = 6?
items.solution: 1. Put t = |x|, so t >= 0; the equation becomes |t^2-5t| = 6. 2. Case 1: t^2-5t = 6 gives t^2-5t-6 = 0, i.e. (t-6)(t+1) = 0, so t = 6 or t = -1. 3. Reject t = -1 (t >= 0); t = 6 gives x = 6 and x = -6. Check: |36-30| = 6. 4. Case 2: t^2-5t = -6 gives t^2-5t+6 = 0, i.e. (t-2)(t-3) = 0, so t = 2, 3. 5. These give x = 2, -2, 3, -3 (each checks: |4-10| = 6, |9-15| = 6). 6. Total: six real values. Answer C.

items.prompt: How many pairs (x, y) of positive integers with x <= y satisfy 1/x + 1/y = 1/6?
items.solution: 1. Combine: (x+y)/xy = 1/6, so 6x+6y = xy, i.e. xy-6x-6y+36 = 36, hence (x-6)(y-6) = 36. 2. If x <= 6 then 1/x >= 1/6, forcing 1/y <= 0, impossible for positive y; so x > 6 and likewise y > 6. 3. Thus (x-6) is a positive divisor of 36 not exceeding 6 (since x <= y): 1, 2, 3, 4, 6. 4. These give (x,y) = (7,42), (8,24), (9,18), (10,15), (12,12) - e.g. 1/10+1/15 = 5/30 = 1/6. 5. Five pairs. Answer: 5

Incorrect. 100 uses the arithmetic mean 50 km/h as the average speed; over equal distances the average speed is the harmonic mean, not the arithmetic mean.
Incorrect. 96 correctly computes the harmonic mean 48 km/h but multiplies it by 2 instead of the 4.5 moving hours.
items.prompt: A man travels from A to B at 40 km/h and returns from B to A at 60 km/h. The round trip takes 5 hours in total, including a 30-minute halt at B. Find the distance AB in km.
items.solution: 1. Let AB = d km. Moving time = 5 - 0.5 = 4.5 hours. 2. Time equation: d/40 + d/60 = 4.5. 3. Common denominator 120: 3d/120 + 2d/120 = 5d/120 = 4.5. 4. So 5d = 540, giving d = 108. 5. Verify: 108/40 = 2.7 h, 108/60 = 1.8 h, total 4.5 h plus the halt = 5 h. 6. Answer D.

explanations: Correct. Migrants are 10% of the final population, so final = 1800/0.1 = 18000; reversing both growths: 18000/(1.2*1.25) = 12000.
Incorrect. 15000 reverses only the first year's growth (divides by 1.2) and forgets the second year.
Incorrect. 14400 reverses only the second year's growth (divides by 1.25) and forgets the first year.
Incorrect. 18000 is the final population before migration - reported without reversing any growth.
items.prompt: A town's population grows by 20% in the first year and by 25% in the second year. At the end of the second year, 10% of the residents migrate out, and the number of migrants is 1800. What was the town's population at the start of the first year?
items.solution: 1. Let the initial population be P. After year 1: 1.2P. After year 2: 1.2*1.25*P = 1.5P. 2. Migrants = 10% of final = 0.1*1.5P = 0.15P = 1800. 3. So P = 1800/0.15 = 12000. 4. Check: 12000 -> 14400 -> 18000; 10% of 18000 = 1800. 5. Answer A.

items.prompt: A and B together can finish a work in 12 days; B and C together in 15 days; A and C together in 20 days. In how many days can A alone finish the work?

Incorrect. 43 is the third position of the cycle (7^3 = 343, which is 43 mod 100) - an off-by-one from reducing 2023 instead of 2024.
Correct. 7^2 = 49, 7^3 = 343 = 43 mod 100, 7^4 = 2401 = 1 mod 100, so the cycle length is 4; 2024 = 4*506 leaves remainder 7^4, i.e. 1.

explanations: Incorrect. 128 counts every multiple of 7 in range without excluding anything.
Correct. Multiples of 7: 128; of 77 (also divisible by 11): 11; of 91 (also divisible by 13): 9; of 1001 (all three): 0. By inclusion-exclusion: 128-11-9+0 = 108.
Incorrect. 117 excludes the multiples of 77 but forgets to exclude the multiples of 91.
Incorrect. 119 excludes the multiples of 91 but forgets to exclude the multiples of 77.
items.prompt: How many 3-digit numbers are divisible by 7 but by neither 11 nor 13?
items.solution: 1. Multiples of 7 from 100 to 999: floor(999/7)-floor(99/7) = 142-14 = 128. 2. Of these, multiples of 77 (also divisible by 11): floor(999/77)-floor(99/77) = 12-1 = 11. 3. Multiples of 91 (also divisible by 13): floor(999/91)-floor(99/91) = 10-1 = 9. 4. Multiples of 1001 (all three): none below 1000. 5. Inclusion-exclusion: 128-11-9+0 = 108. Answer B.

explanations: Incorrect. 2/15 = C(4,2)/C(10,2) is the unconditional probability of drawing two reds - it ignores the given condition entirely.
Incorrect. 1/3 conditions on the FIRST ball being red (then 3/9 for the second) instead of the stated at-least-one-red condition.
Incorrect. 4/5 is the complement - P(not both red | at least one red) - reported instead of the asked probability.
Correct. Favourable pairs (both red) = C(4,2) = 6; eligible pairs (at least one red) = C(10,2)-C(6,2) = 45-15 = 30; so 6/30 = 1/5.
items.prompt: A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. Given that at least one of the drawn balls is red, what is the probability that both balls are red?
items.solution: 1. Total pairs: C(10,2) = 45. Both-blue pairs: C(6,2) = 15. 2. Pairs with at least one red: 45-15 = 30 (the conditioned sample space). 3. Both-red pairs: C(4,2) = 6. 4. Required probability = 6/30 = 1/5. 5. Answer D.
